subject: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
REFUTER PASS. VERDICT RETAINED AT DIVERGES, AND THE DEFECT IS WIDER THAN THE ADJUDICATOR RECORDED.

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.3 "If argument-1 is a date format, the contents of argument-2 shall be a valid date in that format." -> OK (§15.48.3 4)). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14), and I read that paragraph IN FULL because it is what forecloses every escape from the finding below: "... results in an incorrect value for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE according to the rules specified in the function definition ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

⛔ CORRECTION - THE WEEK-DATE CRASH WINDOW IS TWO DAYS WIDE, NOT ONE. The adjudicator cited only "9999W527". I recomputed .NET's ISOWeek.ToDateTime arithmetic by hand: 9999-01-04 is a MONDAY, so correction = 1 + 3 = 4 and ordinal = 52*7 + d - 4 = 360 + d, evaluated as `new DateTime(9999,1,1).AddDays(ordinal - 1)` against a 365-DAY year. d=5 gives 9999-12-31 (integer date 3,067,671, the §15.5.2 maximum - CORRECT and, usefully, the exact boundary the landed FORMATTED-DATE row pins as "9999W525"); d=6 gives 10000-01-01 and d=7 gives 10000-01-02, BOTH past DateTime.MaxValue, and BOTH throw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule passes for both: 9999 > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7. So "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W526" AND "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W527" are both PERMISSIBLE DATA that abort the run unit with a raw CLR stack trace - neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition, where §15.3 rule 14 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. The extended forms "YYYY-Www-D"/"9999-W52-6" and "9999-W52-7" fault identically (same Analyze leg).

CORROBORATION, NOT INHERITANCE: the landed AR-15.79.3-5 RAN this input against the sibling and its own sweep records `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` as verified crashing identically. I re-derived it here from the code and the calendar arithmetic, and extended it to d=6, which no prior record had.

ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX - bound-check the week-date reconstruction in Analyze. Do not count this row, AR-15.48.3-5 and AR-15.79.3-5 as three queue items. THE LOW BOUNDARY IS CLEAN and I checked it rather than assuming it: 1601-01-01 is a Monday and lies in ISO 1601-W01, so ISO 1601-W01-1 = 1601-01-01 = integer date 1, and no week date can underflow the epoch.

test-ref EMPTY: no test, golden or corpus program feeds this function an INVALID argument-2 at all, so neither the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION path nor the crash is pinned anywhere. EDITIONS from the standard (Annex E carries no occurrence of the name), not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.
